cat > enrichment/bible/work/s087/discovery/prepared-20261005/87_2/luna/list.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.1.3	creation by command	The commentary grounds praise in the Creator's work rather than a remote epithet; Genesis has light come to be at God's spoken command, giving a concrete scriptural scene of creation by word.
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.2.7	formed earthling and breath	The commentary reads 87:2 as including the listener's body and later discusses form before spirit; Genesis depicts YHWH forming the human from soil and breathing life into him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.1.31	completed creation called very good	The commentary hears خلق and سوى as making and completing a fitting whole; after the six days God sees all that he made as very good, an explicit judgment on completed form.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.148.5	praise the Name because he commanded creation	The commentary attaches praise of the Lord's Name to the deeds that identify him; this praise summons creation to praise that Name because he commanded and they came to be.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Neh.9.6	creation in a worship litany	The commentary treats glorifying the Name as grounded in works; Nehemiah's prayer names the maker of heavens, earth and sea, says he gives life to all, and ends with heaven's host worshiping.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.12	measures of waters, sky and mountains	The commentary holds together creation, measured proportion and the ordered heavens; Isaiah asks who measured the waters, spanned the heavens and weighed the mountains, making cosmic order the Creator's work.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.38.5	earth measured and line set	The commentary's artisan measures before cutting, while the Creator needs no model; Job's question about who set earth's measures and stretched its line makes cosmic measurement a divine act.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.45.18	earth formed to be inhabited	The commentary says the Most High is known inside his work, not moved beyond the sky; Isaiah says the maker formed the earth to be inhabited rather than leaving it empty.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.1	blessing the Lord in view of his works	The commentary's opening links praise of the Name to the deeds that reveal the Lord; this psalm blesses YHWH and immediately describes his majestic ordering of light and heavens.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.14	grass made for people and animals	The commentary connects creation's ordering with pasture as provision for people and livestock; the psalm says God makes grass grow for cattle and plants for human use.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.29	withdrawn breath and returning dust	The commentary holds completed form beside aging and decay; the psalm says creatures die and return to dust when God hides his face and takes away their breath.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.30	breath creates and renews the earth	The commentary connects bodily formation, breath and the later reversal of creation; this verse says God sends his spirit, creatures are created, and the face of the ground is renewed.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.14	praise for a wonderfully made body	The commentary says the hearer can find the Creator's work in their own body; the psalmist praises God because he is wondrously formed, joining bodily making directly to praise.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.16	unformed substance and numbered days	The commentary's womb discussion treats the body as shaped before its life unfolds; the psalmist says God's eyes saw his unformed substance and his days were written before they came.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.17	God's thoughts beyond counting	The commentary moves from the body as evidence of its Maker to the Maker's knowledge; in the same psalm, God's thoughts are too many to count, extending the creation scene into divine knowledge.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.10.8	hands fashioned and shaped the speaker	The commentary compares creation to measured craft while denying the Creator's dependence on a pattern; Job addresses God as the one whose hands fashioned and shaped him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.10.10	embryonic shaping like milk and curd	The commentary develops the body collected and ordered in the womb; Job depicts conception through the concrete sequence of pouring him out like milk and curdling him like cheese.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.10.11	skin, flesh, bones and sinews	The commentary's body image is one of parts brought into proportion; Job lists skin, flesh, bones and sinews as God's work in forming him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.1.5	formed in the womb and appointed to a task	The commentary links measured making with an apt direction; Jeremiah says God knew, set apart and appointed him before birth, joining prenatal formation to a particular vocation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.12.1	Creator forms the human spirit within	The commentary extends proportioning from the body to inward life; Zechariah names the one who forms the human spirit within as the maker of heavens and earth.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.31.15	one Maker forms master and servant in the womb	The commentary locates the Creator's trace in the listener's body; Job says the same maker formed both him and his servant in the womb, giving shared creation an explicit social consequence.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.11.5	unseen formation of bones in the womb	The commentary stresses that bodily formation exceeds human observation; Qoheleth compares the unknown development of bones in a pregnant woman's womb with God's work.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.6	sinews, flesh, skin before breath	The commentary discusses a formed body awaiting the breath of life; Ezekiel's dry-bones vision orders sinews, flesh and skin before breath, making restoration follow a bodily sequence.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.10	breath makes the assembled bodies live	The commentary joins completed form to life-giving breath; in Ezekiel's vision the bodies stand alive only after breath enters them.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	WLC:Ezek.37.14	bones interpreted as the restored house of Israel	The commentary's womb-and-breath sequence can sound solely bodily; Ezekiel explicitly interprets the assembled bones as all Israel restored to its land, giving the same image a national rather than anatomical referent.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.94.9	formed senses imply the Maker hears and sees	The commentary uses the body as a trace of the Creator's work; the psalm asks whether the one who planted the ear cannot hear and formed the eye cannot see, drawing divine knowledge from bodily design.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.33.15	God fashions every heart	The commentary develops proportioning beyond visible form to inward character; this verse says God fashions the hearts of all and attends to their deeds.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.6	the maker who made and established Israel	The commentary identifies the Lord by what he does; Moses asks whether YHWH is Israel's father and maker, the one who made and established them, making creation grounds for covenant loyalty.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.3	God rides the clouds as his chariot	The commentary contrasts the Most High with a being transported beyond the sky; the psalm pictures YHWH riding the clouds, a concrete image for comparison whose own setting celebrates his power over creation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.33.26	God rides the heavens to aid Israel	The commentary says the Most High is known by works rather than carried beyond the sky; Moses' blessing pictures Israel's God riding the heavens to help them, a contrasting sky image framed as protective nearness.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.3	prepare a straight way for YHWH	The commentary joins making complete to the straight road of guidance; Isaiah calls for a highway in the wilderness for God, turning a straightened path into preparation for his arrival.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.4	valleys raised and rough ground leveled	The commentary gives سوى both completion and straightening, then links it to a road; Isaiah's next verse levels valleys and mountains and makes rough country a plain.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.16.11	just balances belong to YHWH	The commentary defines the سوى family through balance between things and protection from excess or deficiency; Proverbs applies that measure to fair weights and says the scales belong to YHWH.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.16.6	YHWH sets the speaker's allotted portion	The commentary explicitly labels an Arabic branch of خ ل ق as a measured share; the psalm says the lines fell to the speaker in pleasant places and YHWH holds his lot, a concrete allotment image without importing it as the ayah's main sense.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.49.2	polished arrow hidden until its mission	The commentary describes an arrow measured, smoothed and aimed as the next ayah's guidance image; Isaiah's servant says God made him a polished arrow and hid him in a quiver until his word was needed.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.51.6	earth wears out like a garment	The commentary develops smoothness as the worn nap of a garment and the leveling of a ruined trace; Isaiah says earth wears out like clothing, while the heavens vanish like smoke.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.7	grass withers under the Lord's breath	The commentary follows pasture from emergence to darkened refuse; Isaiah says grass withers when YHWH's breath blows on it, making the created pasture's transience explicit.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.78.15	water given from split rock	The commentary's rock image is a hollow that catches and holds rainwater; the psalm recalls God splitting rocks in the wilderness and giving drink from the depths, a related but reversed movement of water from rock.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.78.16	streams from the cliff	The commentary describes a hollow in stone retaining water that would otherwise run off; this verse says God brought streams from the rock and made waters flow down like rivers.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.17.6	water comes out of the struck rock	The commentary's rock-and-water image makes stone a place where water is retained; at Horeb God tells Moses to strike the rock, from which water comes for the people.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.24.27	blessing after God guides a journey	The commentary joins travel, a mount and remembering the Lord's favor; Abraham's servant blesses YHWH after recognizing that God led him on the way to his master's kin.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.20.8	horses contrasted with invoking God's Name	The commentary places remembrance of the Lord on a rider's back; the psalm contrasts those who trust chariots and horses with those who invoke YHWH's Name.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.115.4	idols are made by human hands	The commentary contrasts the Creator's unmodeled work with human fabrication and false worship; this psalm names silver-and-gold idols as human handiwork.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.115.5	idols have mouths but cannot speak	The commentary rejects the creature's fabricated claim as a counterfeit of the Creator; the psalm's handmade images have mouths that cannot speak and eyes that cannot see.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.115.8	makers become like their idols	The commentary says a lie made by a creature imitates the Creator's act but has no reality; the psalm says idol-makers and trusters become like the speechless images they fashion.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.44.13	measured carving made into a human likeness	The commentary contrasts a human artisan who measures and cuts with the Creator who needs no prior model; Isaiah describes the woodworker measuring and carving an image in human form.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.44.15	one piece of wood becomes fuel and an idol	The commentary exposes created objects as poor substitutes for their Maker; Isaiah says the same wood supplies fire and is also made into a god for worship.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.44.17	the remnant of wood is called a god	The commentary's created-versus-counterfeit contrast turns on the maker's false claim; Isaiah's image-maker bows to the leftover wood and asks it to save him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.44.24	Creator stretches the heavens alone	The commentary says the Lord is known by works and needs no model or partner; Isaiah names YHWH as maker of all things who stretches the heavens alone.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.10.12	earth established by wisdom and understanding	The commentary presents creation as measured and completed work; Jeremiah says God made earth by power and established the world by wisdom and understanding.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.10.14	idol-makers' images are false and breathless	The commentary contrasts true creation with fabricated claims; Jeremiah says the images made by craftsmen are a lie and have no breath.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.10.16	Maker of all versus worthless idols	The commentary grounds praise in the one who truly creates; Jeremiah contrasts the portion of Jacob, who made all things, with idols that are not like him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.46.3	God bears Israel from the womb	The commentary's riding image places a human on an animal; Isaiah reverses the carrying relation by portraying God as the one who has carried Israel from birth.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.46.4	God carries Israel through old age	The commentary connects formed bodies with later aging and wear; Isaiah promises that the God who carried Israel from the womb will carry them even into old age.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.9.9	the humble king comes riding a donkey	The commentary describes a rider settling on an animal and remembering the Lord; Zechariah's king arrives humbly on a donkey, a royal riding scene whose Gospel reception adds public praise.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.21.5	Jesus enters as king on a donkey	Matthew applies Zechariah's donkey-riding king to Jesus; beside the commentary's rider who praises the Creator of the mount, the difference is that this crowd welcomes the rider as king.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.21.9	crowd blesses the one who comes in the Lord's Name	The commentary has the mounted worshiper say praise to the Creator who subjected the animal; Matthew's crowd blesses the arriving king in the Lord's Name, shifting the praised figure while retaining the liturgical formula.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.46.5	Hebrew שוה, making equal	The commentary labels سوى as a root of balance and equality; Hebrew שוה here asks whom one can make equal to YHWH, showing a cognate's use in rejecting any rival image without fixing the Qur'anic verb's sense.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Gen.27.11	Hebrew חלק, smooth skin	The commentary explicitly labels خ ل ق B008 with a secondary smoothness sense; Jacob calls his own skin smooth here, a possible cognate with Hebrew חלק that illustrates the dictionary branch but does not replace the ayah's creation sense.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.51.12	create a clean heart and renew the spirit	The commentary extends proportioning from the body to the soul's moral direction; this prayer asks God to create a clean heart and renew a steadfast spirit, making inner ordering a new creation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.2.11	Moses acts when he has grown up	The commentary says the root family can name a man's completion of youth and relates this to Moses receiving wisdom when mature; Exodus marks Moses' adulthood before he goes out to his people.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.34.7	Moses' strength remains at 120	The commentary connects ordered bodily life with aging's reversal; Deuteronomy presents Moses at 120 with undimmed eye and undiminished vigor, a specific counterexample to simple physical decline.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.4.2	neither add to nor subtract from the command	The commentary mentions a separate Arabic form for omitting a letter and places it beside the promise of recitation without forgetting; Moses likewise forbids adding to or subtracting from God's command.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.36.23	the king cuts and burns the scroll	The commentary's secondary root sense is dropping a letter from scripture; Jeremiah depicts Jehoiakim cutting the divine scroll with a knife and burning it, a concrete opposite to preserving recitation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.14	God's spirit restores Israel to its land	The commentary links formed body, breath and guidance; Ezekiel's own interpretation says God will put his spirit in Israel and settle them in their land, turning bodily animation into communal restoration.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.27.11	Jacob's smooth skin and the source commentary's branch label	The commentary labels خ ل ق B008 as smoothness; Hebrew חלק here describes Jacob's skin as smooth, a possible cognate in its own context, though the relation of the roots is uncertain and is not the verse's main claim.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.4	terrain made level for the road	The commentary links the root سوى to straightness and a fitted path; Isaiah's road-preparation image levels the landscape so that the way is made plain.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.3.5	valleys filled and crooked roads straightened	Luke applies Isaiah's leveling image to preparation for God's salvation; it gives the commentary's link between completed form and a straight path an explicit prophetic and ethical setting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.3.6	all flesh sees God's salvation	The commentary says the Creator's work is witnessed in the hearer's body; Luke's next line says all flesh will see God's salvation, widening the prepared road to a universal audience.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.10	rain makes the earth bud and seed grow	The commentary connects ordered creation with water, pasture and provision; Isaiah says rain waters the earth, makes it bud and supplies seed and bread, giving a specific scriptural path from creation to food.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.6.26	birds fed without sowing or harvest	The commentary treats created life as provision for people and animals; Jesus points to birds that neither sow nor reap yet are fed by the Father, a specific ethical inference from creation's ordering.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.4.28	grain grows through stages to full ear	The commentary describes a shoot strengthening, thickening and standing on its stalk; Mark's seed parable likewise names the ordered sequence of blade, ear and full grain.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.24	Creator is not contained in human temples	The commentary says the Most High is not carried beyond the sky and is known by his works; Paul says the Maker of the world does not dwell in temples built by human hands.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.25	God gives life and breath rather than receiving service	The commentary contrasts the Creator with creatures and formed objects; Paul says God is not served by human hands but gives all people life and breath.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.26	nations receive appointed times and boundaries	The commentary's creation includes measured portions and subsequent guidance; Paul says God made every nation and fixed its times and boundaries, then connects those limits to seeking God.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.27	humans are meant to seek God who is near	The commentary links a made and proportioned creature to guidance; Paul says the nations' appointed setting is so they might seek God, who is not far from each person.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.29	divinity is not gold, stone or human craft	The commentary contrasts the Creator with images that creatures fabricate; Paul says divine nature cannot be like gold, silver or stone shaped by human art and imagination.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.1.3	all things came to be through the Word	The commentary stresses that the Creator needs no prior mold; John says all things came to be through the Word and not one created thing came to be apart from him.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.1.16	all things created through and for Christ	The commentary's objectless verb is said to encompass all creation; Colossians names visible and invisible things and every rank as created through and for Christ.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.4.11	worship because God created all things	The commentary grounds the command to glorify the Name in God's creative deeds; Revelation's heavenly worship says all things exist because God willed and created them.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.3	visible things made from what is not visible	The commentary says خ ل ق can cover originating without a model as well as bringing forth from something; Hebrews says the visible order was not made from visible things, making the unseen-origin reading explicit.
strong	tevrat	motif	2 Maccabees 7:28	God made heaven and earth from what did not exist	The commentary preserves creation both without a prior mold and from something else; the mother in 2 Maccabees explicitly tells her son that God made heaven and earth not from existing things.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 11:17	world formed from formless matter	The commentary allows both creation without an exemplar and making one thing from another; Wisdom describes God's hand forming the world from formless matter, a distinct ancient Jewish account of the latter possibility.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 11:20	all things ordered by measure, number and weight	The commentary's measuring artisan image develops creation as proportion rather than decoration; Wisdom says God arranged all things by measure, number and weight.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 42:24	paired works and nothing incomplete	The commentary defines سوى as balance between things and protection from excess or deficiency; Ben Sira says all things are in pairs and God has made nothing incomplete.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 42:25	one work confirms the good of another	The commentary says a proportioned thing is fitted in relation to other things; Ben Sira adds that one work confirms another's good and that this ordered whole displays divine glory.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 9:1	God made all things by his word	The commentary joins the Creator's work to a command that needs no tool or mold; Solomon's prayer names God as the one who made all things by his word.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 9:2	human formed by wisdom	The commentary's bodily formation becomes a human made in fitting relation to the world; this prayer says God formed humanity by wisdom.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 9:3	human appointed to govern creation	The commentary links making to the apt direction that follows; Solomon asks for wisdom to govern the world and judge rightly, making the human creature's purpose explicit.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 15:14	created humans retain choice	The commentary pairs creation with guidance without describing humans as inert; Ben Sira says God created humans and left them in the hand of their own counsel, making moral agency explicit.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 15:16	life and death set before human choice	The commentary develops measured creation and a way to be followed; Ben Sira says fire and water are set before the hearer to choose, clarifying that guidance still addresses an agent.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 15:17	life or death according to the choice	The commentary's creation-and-guidance sequence can be read alongside human response; Ben Sira says life and death are before each person and what they choose is given to them.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 33:10	all humans from earth, then distinguished	The commentary moves from common creation to each creature's measured share; Ben Sira says all humans come from earth and then describes the Most High distinguishing their ways.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 33:13	humanity as clay in the Maker's hand	The commentary's artisan measures material before shaping it; Ben Sira directly compares the human being in the Maker's hand to clay in the potter's hand.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 33:15	opposite works set against one another	The commentary describes balance and its contrary, flattening and decay; Ben Sira says the works of the Most High stand in pairs, one opposite the other.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Targum Onkelos on Genesis 2:7	living soul rendered speaking spirit	The commentary extends bodily making toward inner capacities and the danger of false speech; Onkelos renders the human's resulting life as a speaking spirit, making rational speech part of the creation scene.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5	one first human, many distinct faces	The commentary's objectless creation includes every hearer's body; the Mishnah says one human was created first, yet no two people resemble each other, grounding shared origin and individual form in human dignity.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Pirkei Avot 3:14	human beloved as created in God's image	The commentary asks the hearer to find the Lord's work in their own body; Akiva's saying makes being created in God's image the reason humanity is beloved.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Genesis Rabbah 8:5	creation debated by Truth, Peace and Righteousness	The commentary contrasts the true Creator with lies fabricated by creatures; the midrash places Truth, Peace and Righteousness in debate over humanity's creation, then depicts Truth cast to earth, complicating the ethical meaning of making humans.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Niddah 30b	fetus taught Torah before birth	The commentary presents the womb as a place where a body is formed for later direction; this rabbinic image says a fetus is taught Torah before birth and forgets it on entering the world, adding a tradition of prenatal moral capacity.
medium	tevrat	motif	1QS III,17–IV,26	two spirits and two human paths	The commentary links inner formation to the later distinction between uprightness and deviation; the Community Rule describes humanity as walking in two spirits, truth and injustice, giving a specific sectarian account of moral direction.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.31.3	God's spirit equips a human artisan	The commentary compares measured craft to divine creation without a model; Exodus says Bezalel is filled with God's spirit, wisdom and skill for craftsmanship, making human making a capacity received from the Creator.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.18.4	potter remakes a spoiled vessel	The commentary's craft image distinguishes a maker's measured work from later wear and failure; Jeremiah shows a vessel spoiled in the potter's hand being remade into another form.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.18.6	Israel is clay in the potter's hand	The commentary portrays creation as exacting work without making it a fixed mold; Jeremiah applies potter and clay to Israel, where the image concerns a people God may reshape in response to their conduct.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.64.8	we are clay and God our potter	The commentary uses human craft to illuminate divine forming; Isaiah turns the same relation into confession and plea, calling Israel clay and YHWH its potter.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.9.20	the formed thing questions its maker	The commentary distinguishes the Creator's measured work from a creature's false judgment; Paul asks whether what is formed can say to its molder, Why did you make me this way?
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.9.21	one potter makes vessels for different uses	The commentary says measured creation makes things fit their purpose; Paul asks whether a potter may use the same clay for different vessels, adding a question of divine choice and human limits.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.18	God places each member in the body as he wills	The commentary describes سوى as parts brought into relation without excess or lack; Paul says God arranged each body member in its place, giving that proportioning a communal consequence.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.24	God composes the body and honors weaker parts	The commentary says a sound whole is made by relation among its parts; Paul says God composed the body and gave greater honor to the part that lacked it, turning proportion into care for the weak.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.25	members care equally for one another	The commentary's balance is not mere leveling but relational fitness; Paul explains that the body is arranged so there is no division and members care for one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.2.10	created for good works prepared beforehand	The commentary connects measured making to guidance along a path; Paul calls believers God's workmanship, created in Christ for good works God prepared for them to walk in.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.16	joined body grows as each part works	The commentary's body image treats completion as a relation among parts; Ephesians describes the whole body joined and held together as each part works, producing growth.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.3.9	humans made in God's likeness	The commentary's praise of the Creator rejects false speech and false worship; James says the same tongue blesses God and curses human beings made in God's likeness, making creation a test of speech.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.1.20	creation makes God's power perceptible	The commentary says the Creator is known in the works rather than beyond the sky; Paul says God's invisible power is perceived through what has been made.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.1.23	Creator's glory exchanged for images	The commentary opposes the one who creates to images made by human hands; Paul describes people exchanging the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal humans and animals.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.1.25	creature worship replaces Creator worship	The commentary says a fabricated lie imitates the Creator's act and misdirects worship; Paul says people exchanged truth for a lie and served the creature rather than the Creator.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 13:1	failure to know God from created works	The commentary says the Lord is identified by what he has made; Wisdom criticizes people who failed to recognize the artisan from the beauty of his works.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 13:5	greatness of works points to their Maker	The commentary makes the Creator's works the basis of praise; Wisdom says the greatness and beauty of created things let observers infer their Maker.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 13:10	handmade images called worthless gods	The commentary contrasts real creation with false objects of worship; Wisdom calls the nations' handmade idols worthless gods and condemns their makers' craft.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 15:7	the potter shapes vessels from the same clay	The commentary's artisan scene measures material into a useful form; Wisdom describes a potter shaping the same clay into vessels for different uses, adding a Jewish reflection on craft and purpose.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 15:16	the maker is mortal but the image has no breath	The commentary contrasts the living Creator with fabricated forms; Wisdom says the maker is mortal and the handmade image has no breath, sharpening the difference between life-giving creation and craft.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.1.10	the Lord laid earth's foundation	The commentary includes the ordered sky and earth in the Creator's objectless work; Hebrews applies the psalm's creation words to the Son, who laid earth's foundation and made the heavens.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.1.11	he heavens wear out like clothing	The commentary develops smoothness as wear that erases the nap of a garment; Hebrews says the heavens will perish and wear out like clothing.
